meta.title: Muse Ic mood lexicon – ranked music-mood descriptors mapped to core moods
meta.howToUse: Free-text search: match the query (and each entry's synonyms) to 'term'; combine 'moods' weights (0..1) across matched terms. valence -1..1, arousal 0..1, brightness -1..1, tension 0..1 are weighted means of the mapped core moods' profiles (music-tuned), not word norms. warrinerNorms (1–9 scale) are word-level reference values from Warriner et al. 2013, included for transparency only.
meta.ranking: score = number of independent source families listing the term (Hevner, GEMS, GEMIAC, Last.fm/Laurier, AllMusic Popular Set/MIREX 2007, Last.fm/MIREX 2009, AllMusic index, Cowen 2020, Spotify, Apple) + frequency bonuses: Laurier 4 most-used tags +3, Laurier top-20 +1.5, least-used −0.5, AllMusic Popular Set +1, GEMS factor term +1, Cowen 13-dimension label +1, MIREX 2009 group size +0.5·log10(songs) for the first 5 tags of a group (+0.25·log10 for the rest), Hu & Downie genre-top mood +0.5. Ties broken by source count then alphabetically. True corpus frequencies are only available for a few terms (Laurier: 'sad' 11,898 uses; MIREX 2009 song counts per group); everything else is cross-source consensus.
meta.mappingNote: term→core-mood weights are compiler judgment informed by which cluster/factor each source places the term in.
meta.origin: 'taxonomy' = attested in at least one visited source; 'compiler' = added for search coverage (no frequency evidence, sources empty).

hevner.title: Hevner (1936) adjective circle, 8 clusters / 66 adjectives, as reproduced in Kato, 'RhythMiXearch', ISMIR 2009, Fig. 2 (Hevner 1936 primary PDF blocked)

gemiac.title: Coutinho & Scherer (2017), 'Introducing the GEneva Music-Induced Affect Checklist (GEMIAC)', Music Perception 34(4) – preprint; Table 1 lists GEMS terms per factor, Tables 2–3 new terms/clusters

gems_musemap.title: Musemap: Geneva Emotional Music Scale (GEMS) – 9 scales, 45 labels; GEMS-25, GEMS-9 (Zentner, Grandjean & Scherer 2008)

gems_wiki.title: Wikipedia: Geneva Emotional Music Scale (9 factors, 3 second-order factors)

laurier2009.title: Laurier, Sordo, Serrà & Herrera (2009), 'Music Mood Representations from Social Tags', ISMIR 2009 (Last.fm: 6,814,068 tag annotations; 'sad' used 11,898 times)

hu_downie_2007.title: Hu & Downie (2007), 'Exploring Mood Metadata: Relationships with Genre, Artist and Usage Metadata', ISMIR 2007 (AllMusic's 179 mood labels; 40-label Popular Set; 5 clusters = MIREX clusters)

mirex2007.title: MIREX Wiki: 2007 Audio Music Mood Classification (5 mood clusters)

mirex2009_tags.title: MIREX Wiki: 2009 Audio Tag Classification – Last.fm mood multi-tag dataset (18 groups, 135 tags, song counts)

hu2009.title: Hu, Downie & Ehmann (2009), 'Lyric Text Mining in Music Mood Classification', ISMIR 2009, Table 2

allmusic.title: AllMusic 'Moods' index (editor-assigned mood labels), Internet Archive snapshot 2025-01-03 (live site blocks automated fetch)

cowen2020.title: Cowen, Fang, Sauter & Keltner (2020), 'What music makes us feel: At least 13 dimensions organize subjective experiences associated with music across different cultures', PNAS 117(4)

spotify_features.title: Spotify Web API reference: Get Track's Audio Features (valence = 'musical positiveness'; energy = intensity/activity) – endpoint now deprecated

spotify_filters.title: Spotify Newsroom (2021): Genre and Mood filters in Liked Songs (moods like 'pump up', 'moody', 'soulful')

apple_browse.title: Apple Music: Browse Categories page (includes Chill, Sleep, Fitness alongside genres)

apple_feelgood.title: Apple Music: Feel Good curator page (playlists 'Good Vibes Only', 'Happy Hits', 'Lowkey', ...)

russell_wiki.title: Wikipedia: Emotion classification – Russell's circumplex model (valence × arousal)

warriner2013.title: Warriner, Kuperman & Brysbaert (2013), 'Norms of valence, arousal, and dominance for 13,915 English lemmas', Behavior Research Methods 45 (supplementary CSV used for word-level reference values)
